content.comment_body: Hello, I am working with a PT-100 3-wire setup that uses a USB temperature transmitter, converting the temperature into millivolts. Can I apply the provided example with my [product_name] PLC, and if so, which ports should the connections be made to? I have downloaded the code in [product_name] Web Editor and it's functioning properly with my [product_name] PLC. The transmitter I am using is described in [url]. Please advise on the correct ports for connecting the + and - wires for millivolt measurement with the above example in [product_name] Web Editor. Thank you in advance. [user_name].
Which [product_name] PLC model are you using exactly? Please provide the complete [article_no].
[product_name] PLC Model: [company_name] [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]). Order: [article_no] placed on [date] through [url]. Thank you.
Which analog input address do you intend to use? AI1 (Pin I7) or AI2 (Pin8)?
The attached solution is for AI1 (Pin7). Ensure that both the transmitter and the [product_name] PLC share the same 24 VDC power supply.

Hello, thank you for the prompt response. I have connected the transmitter + to the PLC +, and transmitter - to PLC AI1 (Pin 7). The reading now displays 200C. Where should I connect the 0 VDC and 500 ohm resistor? Thank you in advance.

It's a 500 ohm resistor, not a register. Connect one end of the resistor to transmitter pin 1 (same as AI1), and the other end to the 0 VDC of the power supply (sometimes labeled M pin on the [product_name] PLC).
